title: U.S. House, District 22
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 22th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: Open, newly drawn seat (Rep. Lois Frankel moved to CD 23). Roster from Florida Politics and NBC6: Casey Askar (R) vs. Pia Dandiya (D). No NPA candidate identified; absence unconfirmed. Sources: https://floridapolitics.com/archives/814079-casey-askar-pia-dandiya-to-compete-for-new-cd-22-seat-after-winning-their-primary-races-tuesday/ ; https://www.nbcmiami.com/news/politics/decision/results-of-floridas-district-22-republican-primary-election/3846233/ ; https://www.nbcmiami.com/news/politics/decision/results-of-floridas-district-22-democratic-primary/3846238/ ; county makeup per WUSF map breakdown. Florida adopted a new congressional map (passed Apr 29, 2026, signed May 4, 2026) that reworked 21 of 28 districts; county descriptions here reflect post-redistricting reporting where found (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-05-06/breakdown-changes-for-florida-new-congressional-map).

candidates.name: Casey Askar
candidates.occupation: Businessman (restaurant franchisee, commercial real estate, energy and construction); U.S. Marine Corps veteran
candidates.background: Casey Askar was born in Iraq and came to the United States at age 7; his campaign says his family fled religious persecution. He joined the U.S. Marine Corps at 18 and later built businesses in franchising (his site cites brands such as Church's Chicken and Dunkin'), commercial real estate, energy and construction; he is a father of seven. He won the crowded Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary for the new 22nd District with about 31% of the vote, ahead of fintech entrepreneur Michael Carbonara (about 19%) and Keiser University vice chancellor Belinda Keiser (about 18%); Marine veteran David Burck also ran. President Trump endorsed him for the general election in September 2026, and the NRCC added him to its 'MAGA Majority' program. The Cook Political Report rates the redrawn district R+4.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Republican primary with ~31% over Carbonara (~19%), Keiser (~18%) and Burck (Florida Politics; NBC6)

candidates.name: Pia Dandiya
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Former Apple executive (public-sector partnerships); former high school principal; former White House Fellow
candidates.residence: Palm Beach Gardens, Palm Beach County
candidates.background: Pia Dandiya, a first-generation American born and raised in Palm Beach County, worked as a public school teacher and became a high school principal in Harlem at age 28; she later served as a White House Fellow and as an Apple executive leading public-sector partnerships in education, health care and state government. She originally launched a campaign against U.S. Rep. Brian Mast in the old 21st District and shifted to the new 22nd after the 2026 map was adopted. She won the Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary with about 61% over attorney Kaysia Earley. The DCCC placed her in its 'Red to Blue' program and her campaign reported crossing $2 million raised. She lives in Palm Beach Gardens with her husband and son.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Democratic primary with ~61.3% over Kaysia Earley (Florida Politics; NBC6)
